- **Database update (FL-1683):** Frameleaf moves from PostgreSQL 19 RC 1 to the final PostgreSQL 19.0. Update Frameleaf Manager to 1.2.25 first; it copies your database to PostgreSQL 19.0 during the Frameleaf update and keeps the old copy until it succeeds. Plain Docker Compose installs: follow "Moving to a new PostgreSQL build" in the Postgres administration docs before starting the new release.
- **Back up your whole server to Frameleaf Cloud from Manager (FL-1665, FL-1667, FL-1668, FL-1669, FL-1670, FL-1672, FL-1673, FL-1679, FL-1689, FL-1690, FL-1692, FL-1694, FL-1695, FL-1696, FL-1697):** Manager can back up your photo server, settings and database to Frameleaf Cloud on a schedule, with a speed limit and a time window. A replacement server can restore everything at once from a list of what was protected, or just the files you pick. Every backup includes Manager's settings and your library's backup keys, and runs on your own time zone. A recovery kit, and an optional locked copy of the recovery key in Frameleaf Cloud, get a new server back; it picks up the old server's backup settings. You can disconnect from Frameleaf Cloud or delete this server's backups, with 30 days to change your mind. On HexOS, Server Backup can protect the NAS's own folders. Server Backup uses your server's existing licence. This is an early preview and is switched off unless you turn it on.
- **Cloud Backup restores by date and folder (FL-1666, FL-1675, FL-1676, FL-1677):** browse a backup as it was on any kept date, restore whole folders or single files, and bring back an earlier version of a file that changed. Uploads can have a speed limit and set hours. File names and contents are encrypted before they leave your server.
- **Bring video projects from other editors into Studio (FL-1542, FL-1543, FL-1544, FL-1545, FL-1546, FL-1547, FL-1548, FL-1550, FL-1551, FL-1552, FL-1566):** import projects from Premiere Pro, DaVinci Resolve, Final Cut Pro, Avid (AAF), OpenTimelineIO and EDL, with each clip matched to its media. You can also send a project back out to another editor.
- **Studio (FL-642, FL-1203, FL-1204, FL-1444, FL-1555, FL-1556, FL-1557, FL-1558, FL-1559, FL-1561, FL-1562, FL-1563, FL-1564):** crossfades and curves for sound, sound channel mapping, colour tools (ASC CDL, lift/gamma/gain, hue curves and LUTs kept with the project), HDR-correct transitions and grading, new transitions, markers with notes, fonts kept with the project, and smoother playback of long clips.
- **Choose what you share with a partner (FL-774, FL-786, FL-837, FL-922):** share only chosen albums, people, folders or dates. Favourite shared photos just for yourself, add photos from a shared album or link to your own library, and give new shared links an expiry date by default.
- **Albums (FL-838, FL-846, FL-869, FL-881):** an album for each folder in a library, kept in step when the folder changes. Move photos between albums, hand an album to someone else, put photos in your own order and add text cards.
- **People (FL-874, FL-864, FL-941, FL-1365):** group people as Family, Friends, Work and more, add a date of passing and private notes, and keep archived photos out of People when you choose.
- **Duplicates and downloads (FL-826, FL-832, FL-1660):** set your own rules for which copy of a duplicate to keep. Frameleaf never suggests keeping a damaged or missing copy over a good one. Downloads can be the original, a full-size JPEG or a smaller web size.
- **Search and Best Photos (FL-976, FL-1597, FL-1653, FL-1655):** find photos that are in more than one album. Visual search answers quickly on large libraries and shows more than 100 results. Best Photos works with the larger search model.
- **Eyes in culling (FL-843, FL-863, FL-891):** each face gets eyes-open and sharpness scores, so you can sort by them and filter out closed eyes when picking from a shoot.
- **More graphics hardware for machine learning (FL-984, FL-997, FL-1001, FL-1715):** smart search and faces can run on an Intel NPU, NVIDIA GPUs on arm64 servers are supported (with an NVIDIA driver that supports CUDA 13), and the Desktop helper can use DirectML on Windows. Desktop helpers set themselves up from the machine learning settings, and several desktops can share the work.
- **Imports and uploads (FL-797, FL-818, FL-849, FL-1030, FL-1661, FL-1662, FL-1685):** a first iCloud sync starts downloading straight away instead of after listing your whole library, and a sync carries on after an interruption. Lightroom ratings, keywords, captions and collections come across. Large phone videos and CLI uploads pick up where they stopped.
- **Imported photo times (FL-1683):** photos imported from Photoview, LibrePhotos, Lychee, Nextcloud, pigallery2, Piwigo and PhotoPrism keep their own local time when your server isn't set to UTC, and exact timestamps keep their fractions of a second. Imports no longer stop with a mismatch on those servers.
- **Bookings (FL-1606):** confirm booking requests from your studio website as they arrive, with an email to the client, and add a Booking section to your website.
- **Guest selfie search on Frameleaf Cloud by default (FL-1605):** when face recognition is set to use Frameleaf Cloud, a gallery guest's selfie is matched there too, with no extra setting. If you keep your photos at home, guest selfies never go to Frameleaf Cloud.
- **Library care (FL-977, FL-1362, FL-1378, FL-1674, FL-1680, FL-1686):** file checks pace themselves instead of reading every photo every night. JPEG repair keeps the whole picture, and earlier repairs that cut photos short are made again. Video playback gets a self-test, and failed restore drills tell administrators.
- **Manager (FL-973, FL-1538):** go back to the version before the last update, with its database.
- **Fixes (FL-1361, FL-1367, FL-1371, FL-1374, FL-1497, FL-1607, FL-1649, FL-1650, FL-1651, FL-1652, FL-1656, FL-1657, FL-1658, FL-1659, FL-1681, FL-1693, FL-1698, FL-1718, FL-1719, FL-1720, FL-940):** the timeline no longer jumps to another month while photos are processing, and shift-click selects a range from the photo you clicked last. Long videos keep their thumbnail. The import bar counts photos. Activity, Memories and Places load faster and look right. Thumbnails from a folder scan start sooner, BMP colours are right, removing an account no longer fails, and the "Nothing lost" totals show by month and account. Live updates no longer blank Boards and library grids, edited videos keep their edited size, and the years chart fits on phones and counts photos from external libraries. Importing from Eagle lets you browse the server for the library folder, a new album opens as soon as you create it, and the library no longer reloads over and over during an upload.
